post.description: Creates a user account, signs the user in and sends a verification email (with MAIL_MAILER=log the email, including the verification link, is written to storage/logs/laravel.log). The tokens are NOT in the JSON body: the response sets two HttpOnly cookies, `access_token` (path /, lifetime JWT_ACCESS_TTL minutes, default 15) and `refresh_token` (path /api/auth, lifetime JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS days, default 30). In Swagger UI the browser stores them, so later calls such as GET /api/auth/me work automatically in the same browser. Rate limited (limiter `auth-register`): 5 requests per minute per IP and 5 per minute per email.

201.description: Account created and signed in. Tokens are set as HttpOnly cookies.

Set-Cookie.description: Two HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies (Secure outside local/testing): `access_token=<JWT>; Path=/; Max-Age=JWT_ACCESS_TTL minutes (default 15)` and `refresh_token=<opaque token>; Path=/api/auth; Max-Age=JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS days (default 30)`.

post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description: Checks the credentials and signs the user in. The tokens are NOT in the JSON body: the response sets the HttpOnly cookies `access_token` (path /) and `refresh_token` (path /api/auth). The browser keeps them, so later calls (GET /api/auth/me, POST /api/auth/refresh, POST /api/auth/logout) work automatically in the same browser. A wrong password, an unknown email and a disabled account all return the same 401. Rate limited (limiter `auth-login`): 5 requests per minute per IP and 5 per minute per email.

200.description: Signed in. Tokens are set as HttpOnly cookies.

Set-Cookie.description: Two HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies (Secure outside local/testing): `access_token=<JWT>; Path=/; Max-Age=JWT_ACCESS_TTL minutes (default 15)` and `refresh_token=<opaque token>; Path=/api/auth; Max-Age=JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS days (default 30)`.

401.description: Invalid credentials (unknown email, wrong password or disabled account).

post.summary: Rotate the tokens using the refresh cookie
post.description: No request body. Reads the HttpOnly `refresh_token` cookie (sent automatically by the browser after login or register, because its path is /api/auth), revokes it and issues a new `access_token` and `refresh_token` pair as cookies. If the cookie is missing, invalid, expired or already used, returns 401 and clears both cookies. Rate limited (limiter `auth-refresh`): 30 requests per minute per IP.

parameters.name: refresh_token
parameters.description: HttpOnly refresh token cookie set by login/register/refresh. Sent automatically by the browser.

200.description: New token pair issued as HttpOnly cookies.

Set-Cookie.description: Two HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies (Secure outside local/testing): `access_token=<JWT>; Path=/; Max-Age=JWT_ACCESS_TTL minutes (default 15)` and `refresh_token=<opaque token>; Path=/api/auth; Max-Age=JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS days (default 30)`.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked refresh token. Both auth cookies are cleared.

schema.example: access_token=deleted; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:01 GMT; Max-Age=0; path=/; httponly

get.description: Returns the current user. Authenticate with the `access_token` cookie (set automatically by login/register in the same browser) or with an `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` header. The bearer header wins when both are present. The access token is short-lived (default 15 minutes): call POST /api/auth/refresh when it expires. Returns 401 when the token is missing, invalid or expired, or the user no longer exists or is disabled.

Target of the link in the verification email. The link is a temporary signed URL (valid 60 minutes) carrying `expires` and `signature` query parameters, so it CANNOT be called by hand from Swagger UI without a real signature: copy the full link from the email instead (with MAIL_MAILER=log the email, including the link, is written to storage/logs/laravel.log). On success or failure it redirects (302) to the frontend at FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?status=success or ?status=invalid (wrong id or hash). An already-verified account also redirects with status=success. A missing, tampered or expired signature returns 403 before reaching the controller. Rate limited (limiter `auth-verify-email`): 20 requests per minute per IP.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: SHA-1 hash of the user's email address.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: Unix timestamp at which the signed link expires (part of the signed URL).

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: URL signature generated by the server (part of the signed URL).

302.description: Redirect to the frontend: FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?status=success when verified (or already verified), ?status=invalid when the id/hash do not match a user.

post.description: Sends a new verification email if the account exists and is not verified yet. Always returns the same generic 200 message so it does not reveal whether the email is registered. With MAIL_MAILER=log the email (and its signed link) is written to storage/logs/laravel.log. Rate limited (limiter `auth-resend-verification`): 3 requests per minute per IP and 3 per minute per email.

200.description: Generic response (same whether or not the account exists).

example.message: If the account exists and is unverified, a verification email has been sent.
The email field must be a valid email address.

email: The email field must be a valid email address.

post.description: Sends a password reset email (link valid 60 minutes) if the email is registered. Always returns the same generic 200 message so it does not reveal whether the email exists. The email contains the reset `token` needed by POST /api/auth/reset-password; with MAIL_MAILER=log it is written to storage/logs/laravel.log. Rate limited (limiter `auth-forgot-password`): 3 requests per minute per IP and 3 per minute per email.

200.description: Generic response (same whether or not the email is registered).

example.message: If that email is registered, a password reset link has been sent.

post.summary: Reset the password with a reset token
post.description: Sets a new password using the `token` from the password reset email (see POST /api/auth/forgot-password; with MAIL_MAILER=log the email is in storage/logs/laravel.log). Does not sign the user in. Returns 422 with a plain message when the token is invalid or expired, and 422 with field errors when validation fails. Rate limited (limiter `auth-reset-password`): 5 requests per minute per IP and 5 per minute per email.

422.description: Invalid or expired reset token ({"message": "Invalid or expired reset token."}), or validation failed (ValidationError with `errors`).

value.message: The password field confirmation does not match.

get.summary: Start a social login (redirect to the provider)
get.description: Redirects (302) the browser to the Google or GitHub consent screen and sets a short-lived HttpOnly `oauth_state` cookie (10 minutes) used to check the callback. Requires the provider's OAuth client id/secret and redirect URI to be configured in .env; without them the redirect fails. Swagger UI cannot follow this cross-site redirect usefully: open the URL directly in the browser address bar instead. Not rate limited. Any provider other than google or github returns 404.

302.description: Redirect to the provider's OAuth authorization page.

get.summary: Social login callback (called by the provider)
get.description: The provider redirects the browser here after consent; it is not meant to be called by hand (it needs the provider's `code` and the `state` matching the `oauth_state` cookie, and configured OAuth keys). On success it signs the user in (creating or linking the account), sets the HttpOnly `access_token` and `refresh_token` cookies and redirects (302) to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?status=success. On failure it redirects to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?status=error&reason=<reason>, where reason is one of: invalid_state (state missing or not matching the cookie), provider_error (the provider exchange failed), email_required (the provider returned no email), email_unverified (the provider email is not verified), account_disabled. The `oauth_state` cookie is cleared on success. Not rate limited. Any provider other than google or github returns 404.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: OAuth state echoed by the provider; must equal the `oauth_state` cookie.

parameters.name: oauth_state
parameters.description: HttpOnly state cookie set by GET /api/auth/social/{provider}.

302.description: Redirect to the frontend with `status` (success|error) and, on error, `reason` (invalid_state|provider_error|email_required|email_unverified|account_disabled) query params. On success the auth cookies are set.

Set-Cookie.description: On success: access_token and refresh_token HttpOnly cookies (see POST /api/auth/login), and oauth_state cleared.

AuthResponse.description: Body of register/login/refresh. The tokens are NOT here: they are set as HttpOnly cookies `access_token` and `refresh_token`.

expires_at.description: When the access token (access_token cookie) expires, ISO 8601.

password.description: At least 8 characters, containing at least one letter and one number.

token.description: Reset token from the password reset email.
